citations.M1: This cannot ship Thursday as planned: ... run the corrected backfill to a verified, reconciled completion as its own change before 0143 is scheduled at all.
citations.M4: prod has `PAID`(5210), `canceled`(1988), `complete`(417), and NULL(149) — those ~7.8k rows get `state=NULL` — normalize case/spelling and add an explicit branch (or hard-fail)
citations.M5: the OFFSET-based pagination shifts as rows leave the `WHERE state IS NULL` set on each UPDATE, so every other batch is skipped — paginate by `WHERE id > :last_id ORDER BY id LIMIT` instead of OFFSET
citations.M6: The whole backfill runs inside one `with conn.transaction()` — nothing commits until the full run finishes, so "safe to re-run" is false on a mid-run crash (all progress lost) — commit per batch.
citations.M7: The `status` grep was scoped to `app/` and missed `jobs/nightly_finance_export.py`, which selects `o.status` and filters on it — it breaks outright once 0143 drops the column
citations.M8: require `SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE state IS NULL` = 0 and a spot-check of mapped values against `status` before running 0143
citations.M9: Staging's own log shows only 1,055,000/2,104,377 rows updated (50%)
citations.M10: 0143 drops `status` with no backup of the pre-migration values, including the anomalous 7.8k rows from #1 — export/archive the column before dropping so there's an actual rollback path.
citations.M11: ~61.4M rows extrapolates to roughly 10-11 hours once the OFFSET bug is fixed to actually cover every row — that doesn't fit inside a same-day rollout window
citations.M12: `ALTER COLUMN state SET NOT NULL` on 61M rows takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for a full-table validation scan on Postgres 15, blocking all reads/writes on `orders`
